title: Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
⭐️ Your Impact:

The European trades are one of the least digitised industries left. Software
penetration sits under 15%, against roughly 70% in the US. The labour
productivity gap runs about 30%. Millions of skilled people spend their evenings
on paperwork instead of the craft they trained for — in the industry that has to
deliver the energy transition.

There is almost no incumbent software to displace. That is unusual, and it won't
last.

smalt replaces the back office entirely rather than selling Meister another tool
to manage. In the last six months that went from a partner app and a dashboard
to around thirty AI agents in production - pricing real jobs, qualifying real
leads, running the operations of businesses whose payroll depends on it working.

These days building thirty agents is easy. Knowing which thirty is what's challenging.

That only comes from being in the Betrieb and talking to the Handwerker.

That's what this role is for.

What you'll do

You'll sit in Handwerksbetrieben - at the Meister's desk, in the van, on site, next to our team -
and watch how the work actually happens. Then you'll come back and build the
thing that fixes it, often multiple times on the same day.

- Spend real time with partners. Not a quarterly customer call. You'll know
  our Meister by name, understand their P&L, and notice the thing they've
  stopped complaining about because they assume it can't be fixed.
- Build across the stack. Python/FastAPI services, Vue interfaces, Flutter
  screens, agent loops, data pipelines - whatever the problem needs.
- Own agents in production. Not demos. Agents that price real jobs, answer
  real customers, and cost real money when they're wrong. Reliability,
  evaluation, structured output, graceful failure.
- Decide what to build. You'll write your own acceptance criteria. Nobody
  here will hand you a spec, and waiting for one is how to fail in this
  role.
- Measure whether it worked. Hours saved per partner, offers that go out
  untouched, leads answered before a competitor picks up. If the number didn't
  move, it didn't work.

What that looks like in practice

In July one of our Meister got an early build of the partner app, ahead of the
general rollout. He tested it between jobs and sent screenshots: from a calendar
appointment he could no longer jump into the project to pull the customer's
phone number. He had a reply in two minutes. Within the hour he'd also asked for
a navigation button - tap the address, go straight to maps.

Neither was news. Both were already being worked on before he hit send.

We aim to be fast, and close enough to the work that we've usually seen the problem before the person living it has to tell us.



✨ What Makes You a Great Fit:

You might be a great fit if you

- Have owned something end to end - architecture through delivery through the
  unglamorous iteration afterwards. We don't count years; we look at what you
  carried.
- Get obsessed with a problem rather than a stack. The tools change every few
  months. The curiosity compounds.
- Would rather ship something that changes a tradesperson's week than win an
  argument about abstractions.
- Actually like talking to customers, and have changed your mind about a feature
  because of something a user said.
- Are comfortable being the least knowledgeable person in a room full of
  electricians, and ask the question anyway.
- Can hold "ship it today" and "this needs to survive two years" in your head at
  the same time, and know which one applies.

Our stack, so you know what you're walking into:

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Celery, Redis
- Frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, PrimeVue
- Mobile: Flutter
- AI: Anthropic, Open source and Google models, vector search over partner and catalog data
- Infra: Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Sentry

We care that you're strong somewhere and unafraid everywhere else. If you've
never written Vue but you've shipped production systems and you learn fast, that
is fine - several of us hadn't either.

What we do look for:

- Production experience with LLM-powered features, and the scars that come with it: evaluation, structured output parsing, context management, error recovery
- A track record of shipping things people actually used
- High agency. You'll get context and constraints, not instructions.
- Raw intelligence paired with a humble mindset

German is helpful and you'll pick some up either way - our partners speak it all day. It isn't a requirement but definitely a nice to have. The the team works in English.


☀️ Why You'll Love Working With Us:

- Top-of-market compensation and a meaningful VSOP package
- Direct access to real users and short feedback loops
- Real ownership, and direct proximity to the founders - and to General
  Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures and Heartfelt
- A team of five engineers who have shipped more in six months than most teams
  do in two years, and who set the pace themselves

title: Talent Partner, Strategic Account Management
description:
Our Mission
Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance?

Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist.

We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world.

We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them.

About the Role

The AI Startups and scaleups we work with have roles they can't fill. Not because they haven't tried, but because they have world-class hiring bars, and it’s genuinely tough.

As a Talent Partner looking after our clients, you own those relationships. You take a role briefing properly, you push back when it doesn't add up, and you become the person a founder, internal talent partner or hiring manager calls before they've even decided to hire. You will also own delivery: ensuring that our clients receive an amazing experience using Dex.

You'll also be a power user of our product. We use Dex on our own hiring every day, and the feedback loop between you and the people building it should be strong.

In this role you will:

  • Own a portfolio of client relationships end to end; brief, delivery, feedback, and everything after

  • Take role briefs / kick-offs that actually hold up. Scope the role, interrogate the requirements, and tell a client when the role is really two roles, or shouldn't be hired at all

  • Run the process on the client side: keep feedback fast, keep interviews moving, keep momentum from breaking

  • Analyse their Dex pipelines with conviction and manage expectations so offers land

  • Negotiate offers with the client. Get people over the line without either side feeling managed

  • Grow accounts. Turn a single search into a relationship; more roles, more trust, more of the hiring plan

  • Be the client's most useful call of the week; delivering market insights, clear pipeline reporting, honest candidate reads, and effective advice

About you

  • You are highly organised, compelling, smart, and driven.

  • You're commercially sharp and comfortable holding your ground with senior people. You'd rather have the awkward conversation early than the expensive one late. You tell great stories, and you know how to engage with a wide variety of different people - such as a first-time founder, a Head of Engineering, or a VP of Talent.

  • You're credible with technical hiring managers and you understand how to be an effective partner to your stakeholders. You know enough about software engineering to be taken seriously, and you're honest about what you don't know.

  • You have an excellent command of talent metrics. You know what good looks like at each stage of a funnel, and you use those numbers to diagnose and address a stalling process. You can walk a client through their own data, show them where they're losing people and why.

  • We're open on backgrounds. Most people who do this well have 2+ years in recruitment (agency or internal) but if you've got the raw ingredients and the drive we want to talk to you. We want people who have excelled in their current and previous roles.

  • We are looking for someone that is incredibly motivated to build an exceptional team, solving a problem that truly matters.

  • Note: We know that talent can't be summed up in a few bullet points. Even if you don't match everything we've mentioned, we don't want that to be a barrier. If you're excited about what we're building, we want to hear from you.

Why this is a great opportunity

Dex represents an opportunity to join a well funded, cash generative business that works with some of the most interesting people and companies in the world.

You'll be building relationships with some of the best AI startups and scaleups on the planet, and helping them hire the roles they care most about.

We're growing fast and are set to more than double in headcount between the UK and US over the next 12 months. This is a team that deeply understands hiring, how difficult and how important it is; you'll have experienced talent leaders around you day to day, and a product team building tools for you specifically.

What we offer

  • Above market base salary plus uncapped commission; we're building a world class team and believe pay should match that ambition

  • Significant equity - we want this to be the last job you 'have' to take

  • Full private healthcare & dental - because life happens and we want to support you

  • Fertility benefits & enhanced parental support

  • Gym membership & wellness benefits

  • Claude tokens - lots and lots of Claude tokens

  • Regular socials, offsites and an annual trip

  • MacBook Pro + team kit

  • "Whatever you need" approach to tools and support

The process

Our hiring process is designed to be transparent and respectful of your time. Here's what you can expect:

  • Hiring Manager Interview: Richard, who heads up Talent Operations at Dex (30-45m)

  • Short Take Home Exercise

  • In person interview

    • Task Review (60m)

    • Culture Fit & Values (45m)

    • Final Interview with Paddy, CEO and Founder at Dex (30m)

By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Humboldt is a subteam of Flex Trading Enablement (Trading Optimisation). We sit at the intersection of commercial energy trading and the green transition, and we own Asset Backed Trading.

Asset Backed Trading went live in March 2026. It already runs in two countries, with more markets and features on the way. There is a lot of room to shape how it is built.

It models trading, ancillary service allocation, and dispatch for EU portfolios of batteries, solar and wind. We take market and position updates from Flex APIs, allocate energy and services that help stabilise the grid such as FCR and aFRR across the portfolio, and disaggregate those decisions to individual sites. We can both help traders make decisions about how to trade, and disaggregate said trades into per-asset dispatch decisions.

This is production software with genuine commercial and operational impact. It not only support key traders' workflows, but also it drives physical asset dispatch and the delivery of grid services, so we care a lot about getting it right. You will work with data scientists and traders to turn prototypes into reliable, well tested services they can trust.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join Humboldt and help shape Asset Backed Trading as it grows into new countries and capabilities.

You will work in a Python monorepo of serverless services: event driven pipelines that ingest market and asset data, build optimisation problems, call solvers, and write dispatch and trading positions back out. You will also help evolve the interfaces with other Flex services and APIs that Asset Backed Trading depends on.

This is a great role if you enjoy:

  • Owning production systems that have to be correct, not just available

  • Shaping a young service

  • Designing event driven architectures (queues, events, lambdas, APIs) that stay understandable as they grow

  • Turning messy domain rules into clear models, interfaces and tests

  • Working through new problems at the intersection of software architecture and energy systems modelling

  • Pairing with specialists (traders, data scientists, platform) without needing to be an expert in their field on day one

  • Raising the bar across software (typing, testing, observability, tooling, and thoughtful refactors), tooling, and ways of working

What you'll do

  • Design, build and operate the Python backend services behind Asset Backed Trading

  • Own event driven flows from trigger to dispatch: queues, lambdas, events, and the Flex API integrations around them

  • Productionise new algorithms and market capabilities, working closely with data scientists so prototypes become reliable services

  • Help with team discovery for new epics, spanning software architecture and energy systems modelling

  • Improve reliability, latency, and operability through testing, monitoring, alarms, and careful refactoring

  • Contribute to infrastructure as code (CDK / CloudFormation) and deployment pipelines

  • Take part in architectural decisions as we grow Asset Backed Trading across EU markets and asset types

  • Support teammates through pairing, reviews, and shared problem solving

  • Help keep a high bar for typed, well tested Python in a domain where silent mistakes are expensive

What you'll bring

We don’t expect everything, but experience in several of these areas will help.

Core skills

  • Strong Python experience

  • Experience building and operating backend services in production

  • Comfort with cloud platforms, ideally AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3)

  • API design and domain modelling for complex business workflows

  • Writing robust, typed, well tested code (pytest, CI, 100% branch coverage, a real interest in catching bugs before production)

  • Strong communication and collaboration with both engineers and non engineers

  • Judgement in ambiguity: you can make trade offs explicit and keep delivery moving

Nice to have / especially relevant

  • Experience in problem solving, modelling, optimisation.

  • Event driven or serverless architectures at meaningful scale

  • Infrastructure as Code (CDK, CloudFormation, or Terraform)

  • Experience with Pydantic, strict typing, and mypy

  • Observability in production (CloudWatch, Grafana)

  • Exposure to energy, trading, optimisation, or other constraint heavy domains

  • Working in a monorepo with shared libraries and multiple deployable services

You do not need a background in energy or mathematical optimisation. Curiosity about the domain and a willingness to learn from traders and data scientists matters more than arriving with grid expertise.

Our tech stack

Backend and services

  • Python 3.13, uv, Pydantic

  • AWS Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3

  • pytest, mypy, ruff in CI

  • Mixed Integer Linear Programs for expressing energy storage problems (owned with data science; we integrate with the solver)

Infrastructure and tooling

  • AWS CDK (TypeScript) and CloudFormation

  • aws-lambda-powertools for observability

  • CI/CD via AWS CodePipeline

  • Grafana dashboards and CloudWatch alarms

Product and analysis

  • Databricks SQL, dashboards and notebooks for reporting

  • Jupyter, numpy, pandas, plotly for investigation

  • Cursor, Copilot, and a healthy amount of custom scripting

How we work

  • Small, highly collaborative team with high trust and high ownership

  • No blame: we learn from mistakes by improving systems and process, not by finding fault

  • Optimise for impact on users

  • Pair when it helps, work independently when it does not

  • Sustainable pace

  • Ship quickly without dropping quality: small PRs, fast iteration, quality built in from the start

description:
Tired of retail pharmacy?

Imagine working in a modern, technology-enabled online pharmacy where you can focus on accuracy, quality and patient safety—without standing behind a retail counter, selling OTC products or being interrupted every few minutes.

No retail counter. No walk-in patients. No OTC. Focus entirely on delivering safe, high-quality pharmacy care.

Modern pharmacy. State of the art renovated premises with onsite Free parking

That's what we're building at Montu.

What is the job?

You will be a central, trusted part of our pharmacy operation at our Winnersh site — the person the team relies on to make sure every medicine that leaves our pharmacy is right. That means accuracy checking dispensed medicines, keeping standards high, and actively contributing to a culture where getting it right the first time is non-negotiable. You will not be managed through every task. You will be trusted to lead, to spot problems before they become incidents, and to raise the bar for everyone around you.

What will you be doing?

  • Carrying out accuracy checks on dispensed medicines, ensuring full compliance with legal, operational and safety standards

  • Taking ownership of the end-to-end dispensing process — not just your part of it

  • Maintaining clear, accurate prescription records and escalating discrepancies without hesitation

  • Actively mentoring junior colleagues and helping to build a team culture rooted in accountability, safety and quality

  • Staying sharp on professional development, best practice and regulatory changes — because you want to, not because you have to

  • Working with pace and purpose alongside the wider pharmacy team to ensure every patient gets exactly what they need, when they need it

What do you need?

  • Level 3 NVQ in Pharmacy Services (ACT) or equivalent ACT qualification

  • Current registration as a Pharmacy Technician with the GPhC — no exceptions

  • Solid, proven experience in a pharmacy setting with a strong track record in accuracy checking

  • Deep working knowledge of pharmacy regulations, policies and SOPs

  • The kind of attention to detail that you simply cannot switch off

  • Someone who communicates directly, takes accountability for their actions, and does not wait to be told what to do

  • A genuine, proven commitment to patient outcomes — not just patient care on paper, but real passion for what happens to the person at the end of the process

What we offer:

  • Part-time hours: We offer 16 and 24 hours per week contract (8 hours per day)

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + 8 bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Private Healthcare

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave

As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. At Montu UK, your work has a direct impact on improving patients’ lives and expanding access to modern medical treatments.

title: Director of Self Serve
description:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10, 000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.


The Role

Self-serve today represents a meaningful part of Paddle's revenue. This role owns the commercial mandate to grow that significantly. Not just to run self-serve, but to build the strategy for where and how it scales, and execute against it.

We're hiring a Director of Self-Serve to take full commercial ownership of Paddle's self-serve motion, running and scaling it as a business line. Self-serve is a material and fast-moving part of our revenue, and it needs an owner who thinks in unit economics, not just funnel metrics.

You'll set the strategic direction, and work across Finance, Product, Engineering, Demand Generation, Partnerships, and RevOps to align everyone behind it. Getting this right is a genuinely cross-functional endeavour, and your ability to bring people with you will be just as important as your commercial acumen.

You'll operate with a small, focused team including engineering capacity. This is a role for someone who wants to build and run the engine hands on, not manage through layers.


What you'll do

Own the line. Carry the commercial number for self-serve end to end, from acquisition through adoption, to revenue and net retention. Own the unit economics, and how they improve.

Set the strategy. Form a clear commercial view of where self-serve creates value, ensure Finance and Product alignment, and translate it into a plan the business can execute against.

Own activation and time-to-value. Evolve who and how we onboard through self-serve, how we nurture them through lifecycle stages, and the in-product experience that gets them to value fast. Increasing volume while decreasing time-to-value, not trading one for the other. You fundamentally approach the self-serve experience as a product, running structured discovery and experimentation, not defaulting to only marketing levers.

Shape the demand. Define the customer profile that makes the economics work and work collaboratively with Demand Generation on the targeting you need, co-owning a single funnel against a shared ICP.

Orchestrate cross-functionally. Codify the work into clear streams with clear owners, influence the Product, Engineering, and Risk roadmaps, and run a regular business cadence that keeps people aligned on priorities and impact.

Deepen partner integrations. Work hand-in-glove with Partnerships to turn distribution relationships into deep well-integrated channels, owning the commercial outcome of partner-sourced volume.

Build and run the engine. Design and run the experimentation, tooling, and tracking to improve funnel codification, time-to-value, activation, and conversion using AI where it raises velocity and quality, applied to the right customer. As the motion scales, you'll shape the team around it.

Make the economics stack up. Working closely with finance you own self-serve pricing and packaging as a lever, to ensure profitable scale.


How you operate

Go get the answer yourself. When something doesn't add up, you pull the data, run the analysis, and don't wait to be handed a conclusion. Self-reliance is core to how you operate, not a fallback when support isn't available.

You interrogate, not just observe. Live the ‘five whys’ principle, with the ability to take a plausible looking number, trend, signal and stress-test it until you've found the actual driver, not the first explanation that fits. You default to hypothesis and experiment before you default to opinion or output, treating the funnel as something to be iteratively shaped, not just optimised within.

Given a mission, you don't let go of it. You have a real hunger to find and unlock value you believe is there, working through blockers, organisational, technical, or data.


We'd love to hear from you if you are

  • Deeply experienced in a PLG or self-serve motion in a high-growth tech business, where you've built and owned the funnel rather than a sales-assisted or enterprise motion, and have been accountable for the number, not adjacent to it.

  • A commercial operator who has owned a revenue line, channel, or segment. Someone who operates in founder mode with the instinct to understand the economics, not just the funnel beneath them.

  • You think like a product manager: prioritizing ruthlessly, scope experiments tightly, and see the boundary between growth and product as something to work across.

  • Fluent at moving from data to a commercial conclusion, with the discipline to separate signal from noise and turn analysis into a clear decision rather than a list of observations.

  • A sharp critical thinker who interrogates the brief rather than taking it at face value, challenges assumptions (including ours), and is as willing to conclude "this isn't where we should be investing" as to confirm the plan.

  • A genuine cross-functional leader who has brought structure to messy, multi-team programmes, influenced roadmaps you don't control, and run the cadence that holds a programme together.

  • A credible presence in front of senior stakeholders up to executive level; you communicate with clarity and authority and can take a room with competing priorities to a clear decision.

  • Equally comfortable operating at altitude and dropping into the detail, and always coming back up with a point of view, not just findings.

  • Able to use AI pragmatically; dynamic onboarding, predictive scoring, real-time segmentation, as a means to commercial outcomes, not an end in itself.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we're committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don't care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you're from. We're more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you'll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don't match every part of the job ad, especially if you're part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there's anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We're committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let's grow together.

Why you'll love working at Paddle

We're a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

  • Paddle for others

  • Paddle together

  • Paddle simply

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

Connecting at Paddle

We're a 'digital-first' company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognise that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

Our Paddle hubs:

  • In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Lisbon, Amsterdam and Dublin

  • In North America: Toronto (Canada)

Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work. To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description.

title: Senior Legal Counsel - Privacy
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The LeoVegas Mobile Gaming Group is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Legal Counsel focused on privacy, to join our dynamic and growing Privacy team. This is a pivotal role within the organisation, instrumental in safeguarding the personal data of our customers and employees, and ensuring robust data protection practices across our diverse brands, entities, and markets.

You will play a leading role in the strategic development and operational implementation of our privacy program, with the opportunity of exploring more general legal and regulatory affairs focused matters, as necessary.


YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR:

  • As Senior Legal Counsel - Privacy, your core duties will include, but are not limited to:

  • Take responsibility for ensuring compliance with all privacy related laws and regulations for assigned entities, brands, and markets within the LeoVegas Mobile Gaming Group.

  • Serve as Data Protection Officer (DPO) for designated Group entities, fulfilling all statutory duties and responsibilities associated with the role, ensuring compliance with relevant data protection laws and regulations.

  • Collaborate closely with other DPOs and internal stakeholders on all pertinent data protection matters, contributing to a cohesive and effective privacy framework.

  • Conduct comprehensive data protection due diligence on prospective and existing business partners

  • Draft, review, and negotiate complex data protection agreements, clauses, and terms.

  • Draft, review, and update privacy policies and related procedures, privacy notices, and cookie policies for the Group and its partners, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and legal compliance.

  • Develop and refine internal procedures and policies to ensure robust personal data protection and GDPR compliance across all business operations.

  • Provide expert legal advice and guidance on a broad spectrum of data protection issues to various business units, senior management, and project teams.

  • Actively participate in and lead data protection workstreams within significant company projects, including mergers & acquisitions (M&As), ensuring privacy by design and by default principles are integrated from inception.

  • Take ownership of and lead major privacy-related initiatives, representing the Privacy team in critical cross-functional company projects and steering groups.

  • Mentor junior team members and contribute significantly to the professional development and knowledge sharing within the Privacy team, fostering a culture of continuous learning.

  • Contribute strategically to the evolution and implementation of the Group's overall privacy program and strategy, aligning with business objectives and regulatory landscapes.

  • Provide assistance and legal advice concerning data subjects' rights requests, ensuring timely and compliant responses.

  • Manage and provide expert advice on customer complaints related to data protection, including conducting thorough internal investigations, drafting submission, and preparing comprehensive reports.

  • Liaise effectively with data protection supervisory authorities and other regulators regarding complaints, inquiries, audits, and other regulatory matters.

  • Handle any data breaches and associated reporting requirements in a timely and compliant manner;

  • Ensure that material data protection risks are escalated appropriately and that regulatory reporting obligations are discharged within statutory timeframes.

  • Proven experience in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex data protection agreements and privacy-related policies.

  • Demonstrated ability to act as a DPO or hold a similar lead privacy advisory role, including managing regulatory interactions.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills with the ability to translate complex legal requirements into practical business solutions.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to advise and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organisation.

  • Ability to work autonomously, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, and evolving regulatory landscape.

  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

  • Any relevant privacy certifications.

title: People Operations Lead
description:
📍 London - Hybrid. 2 days per week in our London office, 3 days remote / work from home (40 hour week)
🚆 Monthly travel to one of our other offices (Sheffield/Lincoln) is essential.
✴ All travel and accommodation costs to non-base office locations are fully covered.

We've spent the last three years transforming how our People Team operates. Now we're looking for someone to own the machine and work out what comes next!

About the role

We're looking for a People Operations Lead to own the operating layer of our People function, managing our People Operations Specialist and reporting directly to our People Director.

This isn't a traditional HR Operations role, and we're not looking for someone to simply keep existing processes running. We want someone who's genuinely curious about how and why things work - someone who spots friction, interrogates the data, challenges the way we've always done things and builds something better.

You'll inherit a strong foundation. Over the last three years we've streamlined manual processes, invested in our People technology and changed the way our People function operates. There's plenty we're proud of - but we're definitely not done!

You'll own our People operations, systems and data infrastructure across the end-to-end colleague lifecycle, making sure the fundamentals run brilliantly while continuously looking for opportunities to simplify, automate and improve them.

You'll also take significant ownership of our reward infrastructure, including quarterly pay reviews, salary benchmarking and banding, benefits and gender pay gap reporting. You'll work closely with our People Partners, Talent, Finance, Payroll and Tech teams, so this is a highly collaborative role with influence across Goodlord.

And increasingly, you'll help us answer a bigger question: what work should technology be doing for us?

We're already exploring how AI and agentic workflows can remove repetitive work across areas such as onboarding, colleague queries, document management, data validation and reporting. You don't need to arrive as an AI expert, but you do need to be excited about the possibilities, willing to experiment and comfortable helping us work out where technology can genuinely make things better.

If you get a kick out of taking something that already works, understanding it properly and making it simpler, smarter and better, we'd love to hear from you.

Who are you

You're probably someone who sees People Operations a little differently.

You care about delivering a brilliant colleague experience, but you're just as interested in the systems, data and processes underneath it.

You don't accept a seven-step process because it's always had seven steps. You'll want to understand why it's there, whether we still need it and what would happen if we did it differently.

What does that mean in practice?

  • You're naturally curious and analytical. You ask good questions, get underneath problems and use data rather than instinct alone to make decisions.

  • You love improving how things work. You've reviewed, redesigned and implemented processes rather than simply inherited and administered them.

  • You're comfortable getting into the detail while still seeing the bigger picture - whether that's interrogating a spreadsheet, configuring a workflow or digging into an HRIS.

  • You're pragmatic, comfortable with ambiguity and a confident collaborator. You can turn an idea into something that actually works and bring people with you when something needs to change.

What we need from you

  • Significant People Operations experience, with evidence that you've owned and designed end-to-end People processes, not simply operated processes someone else created.

  • Hands-on experience owning or significantly shaping People systems and data using a modern tech stack, including an HRIS (we use Personio, but we're of course open to others!) and/or headcount planning systems, alongside strong analytical and advanced Excel skills.

  • Experience across reward and benefits, ideally including ownership of pay review cycles, salary benchmarking and banding, benefits and gender pay gap reporting.

  • A track record of continuous improvement - spotting friction, getting underneath the root cause and leading meaningful changes that have made processes simpler, better or more scalable.

  • An active interest in AI and automation and how they can change the way People teams operate. You'll be comfortable experimenting with new tools and ways of working.

title: Executive Audience Manager
description:
About The Alliance

When it comes to building world-class professional communities, The Alliance is leading the way. From Product Marketing and Sales Enablement to Product-Led Growth, AI, Customer Success, and CMOs, we're home to some of the most engaged and influential communities in the industry.

With 160,000+ professionals across our communities and a constant stream of content, courses, events, and memberships, we help our members learn, connect, and grow. Our executive events are a key part of that mission—bringing together senior leaders to share insights, tackle industry challenges, and build meaningful relationships.

Every year, we engage attendees, speakers, partners, and members from some of the world's leading organisations and fastest-growing start-ups, including TikTok, Microsoft, Peloton, and Uber.


The Role

Our executive programmes only work if the right people are in the room. As Executive Audience Manager, you own the audience for our invitation-only events. You identify the senior leaders who belong at each table, you earn their attention, and you convert that attention into confirmed, qualified, high-value attendance. Our Content and Events teams build the experience. You build the room.

You'll work closely with Commercial, Partnerships and Marketing, and you'll own the executive relationship end to end: from first touch and qualification, through confirmation and show-up, to the follow-up that turns a one-time attendee into a long-term member of the community.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define the target audience: Work with Commercial and Marketing to translate each event's brief into a clear, named list of the executives who should be there, and the seniority and profile criteria that qualify them.

  • Build and run executive outreach. Own multi-channel campaigns across personalised email, LinkedIn, phone, referrals and warm introductions. Own the volume, own the follow-up, own the pipeline.

  • Qualify rigorously. Confirm seniority, decision-making authority, budget relevance and peer fit before an invitation is issued. Protect the quality of the room, including when that means saying no.

  • Convert and hold attendance. Manage invitations, confirmations, pre-event communications and reconfirmation with a white-glove touch. Minimise drop-out and keep every confirmed guest engaged right up to the day.

  • Hand over cleanly. Give the Events and Content teams a fully briefed, confirmed audience ahead of every event, with the profile detail they need to run the room well.

  • Retain and grow. Maintain relationships after the event, drive repeat attendance, and grow our executive communities through referrals and exclusive engagement opportunities.

  • Share what you learn. Capture commercial and market insight from your conversations, keep the CRM clean and current, and give internal teams warm, well-briefed handovers.

What Success Looks Like: You are measured on the quality and reliability of the audience you deliver.

Success means every event opens with a full room of genuinely senior, genuinely relevant executives who wanted to be there. It means low drop-out, high repeat attendance and a growing pool of executive relationships that belong to The Alliance rather than to any single campaign. It means Commercial and Event teams who trust that when you say the audience is secured, it is secured. And it means attendees who accept the next invitation because the last one was worth their evening.

What We're Looking For

  • Relevant experience could be in executive audience acquisition, B2B events, executive networking, partnerships, business development, or community building.

  • Comfortable approaching, engaging and holding the attention of C-suite and senior decision-makers, mostly by email, LinkedIn and phone.

  • A closer's instinct for follow-up. You are persistent without being a nuisance, and you don't lose people in the gap between interest and confirmation.

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills. Your outreach reads like a person, not a template

  • Highly organised with the attention to detail that white-glove executive handling demands.

  • Comfortable owning a target and working to a deadline that does not move, because the event date does not move.

  • Experience using CRM platforms, LinkedIn, and outreach tools is an advantage.

What This Role Is Not

To help you self-select: this is not an event production, logistics or on-site hosting role. You will not be sourcing venues, running the operational build or working the room on the night. Our Events team owns all of that. This is an acquisition and relationship role, and your week is spent in outreach and conversation with senior executives.

Benefits: We believe exceptional people deserve exceptional support.

Time Off:

  • 34 days' annual leave, including UK Bank Holidays.

Equipment & Culture

  • New tech setup including laptop, screen, mouse, and keyboard.

  • A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive working environment.

Community & Inclusion

At The Alliance, we're committed to creating a workplace that is free from discrimination and bias, where everyone has equal opportunities to succeed and contribute.

We know our work here is never done, and we continue to strive for a more inclusive environment every day.

If you're worried you don't meet every requirement listed, don't let that stop you from applying. Unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are essential to our ability to innovate and grow, so if you think you'd be a great fit, we'd love to hear from you.

We are The Alliance—in more ways than one.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
Procurement and supply chain is a $3 trillion market still running on outdated systems and manual processes. Magentic is changing that.

We’re building a new generation of agentic AI that works inside the world’s largest and most complex organisations, backed by Sequoia and built by a team from OpenAI, Meta, Revolut, NASA and McKinsey. We’re early, moving fast and already solving real problems for global enterprises.

As a Deployment Strategist, you’ll be at the heart of making that happen. You’ll take what we build and turn it into real-world impact for our customers, owning engagements from initial scoping through to live deployment.

You’ll sit at the intersection of product, commercial and customer, figuring out what needs to be built, how we make it work and how we deliver meaningful outcomes. You won’t just be deploying Magentic, you’ll help shape how we work with customers as we scale.

What You’ll Do

You’ll have a huge impact on both Magentic’s commercial success and our product direction. This is a rare opportunity to help build a rocket ship. As we grow, you could develop into product management or engineering, into a leader in our customer engineering space, even into sales, as you discover your strengths and interests.

  • Own deployments end-to-end—design the rollout strategy at household-name enterprises, run the programme, and change course decisively when the approach isn't landing.

  • Hold the senior relationships—be the Director and VP sponsor's first call, run steering governance, and take on the difficult conversations.

  • Find the value nobody has scoped—go looking beyond the signed scope, prove new use cases with the customer, and build the case for what we sell them next.

  • Define best practice for AI deployment—set the bar on your deployments, and turn this into processes that the rest of the org can use to scale.

  • Shape our roadmap—bring product and engineering the problem, the customer evidence, and a view on what we should build.

You Might Be a Great Fit if You

  • Have 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing delivery or product role

  • Have managed complex, multi-stakeholder projects at senior levels and kept them moving when priorities shifted

  • Think commercially: you track outcomes, not just activities, and you understand how successful deployments translate into revenue

  • Are energised by early-stage ambiguity — you can create structure where none exists and make decisions with incomplete information

  • Communicate exceptionally well, both in the room with a VP and in a written handover to a colleague

Bonus Points

  • Have experience deploying AI, automation, or data products inside large organisations

  • Are familiar with procurement, supply chain, or finance functions in enterprise settings

Compensation and Benefits

At Magentic, we recognise and reward the talent that drives our success. We offer:

  • Competitive Equity: play a real part in Magentic’s upside

  • A salary of £100-110k

  • Enhanced parental leave

  • 25 days holiday exc bank holidays, plus an extra day for our Christmas shutdown

  • In-office lunches provided

  • Salary sacrifice pension and nursery schemes

  • Hybrid London HQ (WFH Thurs and every other Tues, with flex if you have appointments etc)

  • Annual team retreat—a fully-funded off-site to recharge, bond, and build

Our Interview Process

We can move quickly through these stages, so let us know if you have any timelines we need to meet.

  1. Initial call (30 mins): this first step is an opportunity for you to hear more about Magentic and the role, and for us to learn more about how your experience aligns with the role.

title: Mechanical Design Engineer
description:

Location:
Concept House, Brackenbeck Road, Bradford, BD7 2LW

Technical Manager

Salary is negotiable and will reflect the successful candidate’s skills, experience and qualifications.

Job Purpose

Debar designs and manufactures bifold door hardware and complete bifold door systems for customers in the UK and international markets. As we invest in future growth and an expanding product pipeline, we are creating a new Mechanical Design Engineer position within our Technical Engineering team.

Our development work follows two complementary routes: collaborating with external systems houses and industry partners to create hardware solutions for their door systems; and developing Debar's own proprietary or white-label bifold and other system solutions for selected global markets.

The role may support either or both routes. The successful candidate will take mechanical components and assemblies from concept through detailed design, prototyping, testing and production, while contributing technical expertise in discussions with customers and partners where required.

Our products integrate precision hardware with aluminium profiles, so sound judgement around tolerances, fit, movement, materials and manufacturing methods is essential.

Key Responsibilities

Product & System Development

  • Design and develop mechanical components, assemblies and product concepts for bifold door hardware and systems, together with other products as required.
  • Work with systems houses, fabricators and industry partners to understand technical requirements and develop hardware solutions that integrate effectively with their systems.
  • Design and develop Debar’s proprietary and white-label bifold and other system solutions for introduction into appropriate global markets.
  • Create accurate 3D CAD models, assemblies, manufacturing drawings, specifications and Bills of Materials.
  • Take designs from initial concept through detailed engineering, prototype, testing, validation and production release.
  • Consider how hardware interacts with aluminium profiles and the complete door system, including alignment, movement, adjustment, load transfer and long-term performance.
  • Carry out tolerance analysis and tolerance stack-ups to achieve reliable fit, function and manufacturability.
  • Undertake appropriate engineering calculations and analysis to substantiate design decisions and product performance.
  • Contribute ideas for future products and provide practical engineering input into product and system opportunities.

Manufacture, Testing & Engineering Control

  • Apply Design for Manufacture and Assembly (DFM/DFA) principles across relevant processes including machining, extrusion, die casting, injection moulding, pressing and mechanical assembly.
  • Work with Production, Quality and the wider Supply Chain to resolve manufacturing, tooling, quality and cost considerations.
  • Support prototype builds, product testing and the structured investigation of issues arising during development and product launch.
  • Maintain drawing revisions and engineering change records, ensuring design changes are controlled and validated.
  • Improve and value-engineer existing products without compromising performance or quality.
  • Refine and value-engineer products during development and launch without compromising performance or quality.

Technical & Partner Collaboration

  • Communicate technical concepts, design decisions and development progress clearly to colleagues, customers, system partners and suppliers.
  • Translate commercial, customer or system requirements into practical, manufacturable engineering solutions.

Person Specification

Essential Qualifications, Skills & Experience

  • Degree, HND or equivalent recognised higher-level qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Product Design Engineering or a closely related discipline. A relevant formal qualification is mandatory and experience alone will not be accepted as an alternative.
  • Relevant professional experience in mechanical design, product design or product development engineering.
  • Strong capability in parametric 3D CAD and manufacturing-ready engineering drawings.
  • Experience designing physical products or components for manufacture rather than CAD modelling alone.
  • Practical understanding of mechanical engineering, materials and manufacturing processes.
  • Strong understanding of Design for Manufacture, dimensional tolerances, engineering fits and tolerance stack-up analysis.
  • Methodical mechanical problem-solving skills and strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to progress defined engineering work independently while contributing effectively to a wider team.
  • Confidence communicating technical information with customers and partners.

Particularly Valuable Experience

Experience in any of the following would be particularly valuable:

  • Fenestration, windows, doors, aluminium architectural systems or other moving door systems.
  • Mechanical or architectural hardware such as hinges, rollers, guides, handles or locks.
  • Small precision components involving aluminium extrusions, castings, mouldings or CNC-machined parts.
  • Product testing, New Product Introduction, value engineering, tooling or supplier development.
  • Autodesk Inventor is strongly preferred; experienced SolidWorks, Creo or comparable CAD users will also be considered. AutoCAD and ERP experience would be beneficial.

Direct experience designing bifold door hardware or systems would be particularly valuable but is not an essential requirement.

Attributes

  • Practical, curious and interested in how mechanical products and systems work.
  • Able to balance product performance, manufacturability, quality and cost.
  • Credible and confident in technical discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Collaborative, self-motivated and comfortable taking ownership of defined projects.
  • Enthusiastic about joining a business investing in product development and future growth.

Working Conditions

  • Full-time, permanent role based primarily at Debar’s Bradford facility, with one day per week homeworking currently available.
  • Occasional travel may be required for supplier visits, product trials, customer projects or testing.

description:
Location: Chancery Lane, London (Office-based 4 days)

The Mission

At Fyxer, we believe the only sustainable competitive advantage for a startup is the quality and speed of execution.

We are looking for a Product Lead who operates like a Staff PM: someone who owns our most important product bets end-to-end, from ambiguous problem space to shipped outcome. You combine sharp product judgment with hands-on discovery skills, and you measure yourself on commercial impact, not output.

We're not looking for someone to write specs and manage a backlog. We want someone who helps us think better, decide better, and ship better. The goal isn't more process, it's higher quality decisions made faster.

You will work directly with our Head of Product, CTO, founders and senior engineers to shape what we build and why.

What you will own

You will not hand anything over. You will own the bet from first insight to shipped impact.

  • Own discovery through delivery for our most important product bets, from early ambiguity to validated direction to launched product

  • Work directly with engineers and founders from the start of any initiative as the accountable product owner, not a coordinator

  • Frame the problem, define the hypothesis, and choose the fastest route to signal: interviews, prototypes, fake doors, experiments, or just shipping and measuring

  • Translate messy qualitative and quantitative signals into clear product direction, then drive that direction through to execution

  • Set success metrics, make the call on when there's enough signal to build, and own the outcome either way

  • Embed structured learning loops into how we operate so insight compounds over time

  • Raise the bar of product thinking across the team: coach others, introduce lightweight frameworks, and get the whole company closer to customers

Who you are

You are a full-stack product thinker.

  • Outcome owner: You connect user behaviour to funnels, retention, and revenue. You think in bets and expected value, not feature lists, and you hold yourself accountable to results.

  • Discovery-strong: Genuinely fluent across qualitative research, behavioural insight, and experimentation. You generate strong signal quickly and pick the right method for the decision at hand, rather than outsourcing the thinking.

  • Engineering partner: You work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, translating insight into crisp problem framing and practical tradeoffs. Engineers want to work with you because you make the work clearer, not slower.

  • Decision oriented: You know when there's enough signal to move. You sharpen hypotheses, clarify thinking, and make confident calls under uncertainty. You'd rather ship and learn than perfect and wait.

  • Force multiplier: Your impact shows up in how the whole team operates. You build repeatable systems for discovery and decision-making that outlast any single project.

The Role

You will be the senior product voice on our most important initiatives, working directly with the Head of Product, CPGO, founders, and senior engineers. This is not a support function. You will be embedded in high impact work from day one, with real authority over what we build and why.

You will operate at speed. We care about generating signal quickly, making informed decisions, and shipping fast. You are comfortable working with imperfect information and tightening your thinking as you go.

You will move fluidly across the full product lifecycle. Some weeks you will be deep in user interviews or pressure testing a major bet, other weeks you will be in the detail with engineers getting something over the line.

You will have significant autonomy. We expect strong judgment, clear communication, and ownership of outcomes.

If there are specific tools you believe are critical to moving faster or generating better signal, we will support that. We want you to design the right setup, not work around constraints.

Why Fyxer?

We are intentional about our team. We believe a small, exceptional team working with extreme focus will always outperform a large, bloated organization.

  • Autonomy: We hire people who want ownership and then we actually give it to them.

  • Velocity: You will be fast-tracked into senior responsibilities far earlier than at a traditional company.

  • Scale: We are on track to hit $100M in revenue by the end of 2026. This is a rare opportunity to join a high-growth rocket ship at the foundational stage.

title: Senior Legal Operations Manager
description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The opportunity

We're hiring our first dedicated legal operations team member to sit at the heart of 9fin's growing Legal Affairs function. This is a broad, hands-on role and a rare opportunity to shape how a scale-up in-house legal team runs from the inside out.

You'll own the operational engine of the team: our contract lifecycle platform (Ironclad, which is deeply embedded across sales, procurement and RevOps), our commercial playbook (and developing non-commercial playbooks), our tech stack (including AI implementation), our front-door (right now, ticketing is done in Linear), our knowledge management (currently spread across multiple systems), our reporting and KPIs, and the tracking and governance around outside counsel spend.

You'll also be a project manager and a hands-on partner to the General Counsel. That includes co-drafting monthly and quarterly business reviews, leading and coordinating cross-functional initiatives (for example M&A diligence coordination, trademark portfolio work, or regulatory readiness workstreams), and holding a high bar for organisation so nothing on a small, fast-moving team drops.

You'll report to the General Counsel and work alongside legal colleagues in London and New York. This is a London-based role and we typically expect the team to be in the office three days a week.

What you’ll work on

Below is the shape of the role, laid out as prioritised by Now, Next and Later so you can see the broad strokes of the path ahead - but by no means is this set in stone. Priorities will move as we learn what's most useful in practice and you’ll have a big hand in shaping this further.

Now

  • Tune legal intake - help us build out the “front door” for legal requests across the business.

  • Partner with Sales, Finance, InfoSec and Procurement to streamline deal-desk and approval processes

  • Support on knowledge management and internal policy administration. Consolidate knowledge, templates, and other information in a clean accessible structure.

  • Build our external legal spend tracker from scratch. Categorise spend, log invoices and quotes, match to matter, and produce a monthly view for the General Counsel.

  • Own KPI reporting improvements against our Ironclad-fed dashboards. Expand coverage into intake, spend, cycle times, and other operational metrics.

  • Own operational and reporting support across the Legal function, including responses to internal stakeholders including Finance, RevOps, and the People team.

Next

  • Get inside and own our tech stack and know it end-to-end - Ironclad, Linear, Google Workspace, Notion, and the AI tools we've adopted or are evaluating.

  • Build, maintain and roll out templates, playbooks and self-serve legal resources so the business can move quickly.

  • Own Ironclad workflow hygiene and adoption end-to-end. Work with the team to clean up metadata and archiving, tighten approvals and signatory workflows, and work with commercial counsel to roll out training across sales, procurement, RevOps and other frequent users.

  • Bring structure and visibility across the team. Keep track of open projects, drive follow-through, and make sure balls do not drop across a small team with a lot of surface area.

  • Maintain our sales contract playbook. Keep it current, propose updates as commercial patterns and RevOps feedback surface them, and make sure the team is actually using it.

Later

  • Partner with the General Counsel to produce meaningful Exec-level reporting.

  • Assist with management of large legal projects on GC instruction. Recent examples include M&A diligence coordination, and trademark portfolio work.

  • Support company secretarial administration.

About you

We're looking for a highly organised operator who is energised by building order out of scale-up complexity. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you do need to have run legal operations end-to-end before. The essentials come first below, followed by preferred experience and the traits we care about most.

  • Highly organised with a systems mindset: You keep the plates spinning and notice when one wobbles. You see the workflow behind the task and design for repeatability.

  • Commercial, action-biased, comfortable with ambiguity: You understand what the business needs from legal, get things over the line without waiting to be asked twice, and you're comfortable being the first hire writing the map as you go.

  • Ironclad or equivalent CLM: Hands-on experience with Ironclad or a directly comparable enterprise CLM (for example Juro, LinkSquares, Icertis, Agiloft, Leah). We are deeply embedded in Ironclad and you will own it.

  • Legal operations track record: At least five years' experience running legal operations, contracts operations or a closely adjacent function (compliance operations, legal project management, or legal chief-of-staff), ideally in a scale-up or in-house legal team that is fast paced and where you can demonstrate ownership.

  • End-to-end project delivery: You have owned legal or cross-functional projects on your own steam, including timelines, risks, stakeholders and outcomes.

  • Reporting and data fluency: You can build clean dashboards, work with a KPI framework, and translate metrics into a story someone can act on.

  • Outside counsel spend or panel exposure: Experience setting up spend tracking, panel management or legal project management would be useful, but we're also open to someone with the capability and appetite to build this from scratch.

  • Builder mentality: Experience as a team’s first or only legal-ops hire, or a member of a small team in the early stage of the build-out of a legal ops function, would be a strong advantage.

Benefits

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

Training & Culture

title: Frontend Engineer
description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our application focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations

Our objective is to organise anyone's life.

 

Role

As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets.

  • Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets.

  • Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications.

  • Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows.

  • Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices.

  • Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies.

  • Deep understanding of frontend architecture, state management, browser APIs, and performance.

  • Experience building highly interactive products such as chat, collaboration, productivity, document editing, calendars, or workspaces.

  • Experience with real-time systems, WebSockets, streaming APIs, or collaborative interfaces.

  • Strong product and UI judgment with attention to interaction details.

  • Able to independently own features from technical design through production.

 

Outcomes

  • Users can communicate, write, organise and collaborate seamlessly across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

  • Complex interactions such as group messaging, editing, scheduling and collaboration feel fast and reliable.

  • AI capabilities are integrated naturally into product workflows rather than added as separate chatbot experiences.

  • Frontend architecture remains fast, maintainable and reusable as ActAI expands into new applications and workflows.

 

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript

  • React.js / Next.js

  • HTML / CSS

  • WebSockets / streaming APIs

  • Node.js

  • REST / GraphQL APIs

 

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world-class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high-quality work and learning.

Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment and execute independently. Our goal is to put in the hands of our users a truly magical product.

 

Interview Process

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us and help bring practical AI benefits to billions of users globally.

Le rôle

Fastned France est en pleine expansion, et en tant qu'Expansion Manager, tu seras un.e acteur.rice clé de cette croissance.

description:
Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Commercial team sits at the centre of Deliveroo’s marketplace—shaping how we serve restaurants, grocers, and new verticals worldwide. From negotiating key partnerships to unlocking new revenue streams and crafting data-led growth strategies, we take on big challenges that move the business forward. If you thrive in fast-paced, commercial environments and want to influence the future of a global brand—this is the team for you.

Editions, our network of delivery-only kitchens, is a key differentiator in France commercial ambition. The Account Management Lead – Editions France role is created as part of a wider reorganisation of the Editions business as part of our regional strategy. The role reports to Paris regional leadership and is designed to combine strategic partner leadership, P&L ownership and organisation building across the Editions network.

The Role

As Account Management Lead – Editions France, you will lead the Editions commercial team for France constituted of Senior Account Managers, Account Managers and Sales Managers. You will be the guardian of the Editions strategy for France, accountable for its coordination and its execution on the ground, growing the performance and profitability of our sites while driving occupancy and the differentiation Editions brings to the French market.

You will own a portion of the Editions P&L. That means holding the commercial scorecard for new kitchens, making financial decisions with a clear view of both partner and Deliveroo profitability, and steering your team's portfolio towards sustainable growth rather than volume alone.

You will be accountable for the development plan for your team, their success and learning curve at Deliveroo; setting the right KPIs and OKRs to monitor the business. Your role will be commercially focused, however Editions is as much a project management discipline as a commercial one: you will work hand in hand with Food Safety, Compliance, Site Construction, Kitchen Layout, Site Operations, Marketing and the International Editions team to bring kitchens live and keep them performing.

 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Editions Strategy & Growth

    • Act as the guardian of the Editions strategy for France, ensuring its coordination across teams and its disciplined execution site by site

    • Lead your team's portfolio strategy, growing the performance and profitability of each Editions site in line with agreed targets

    • Develop the business so that it fits within, and contributes to, the wider regional strategy, bringing the specificity of the French network to regional and international forums

    • Build and deliver joint business plans with restaurant partners, identifying growth and profitability opportunities, defining mutual goals and finding compelling ways to solve them (menu optimisation, virtual brands, pricing, packaging, catchment expansion)

    • Coordinate with the Media team to identify and negotiate revenue opportunities to generate additional value from Editions sites

  • Occupancy & Commercial Performance

    • Own the occupancy trajectory of the French network, partnering closely with Local teams to positively drive occupancy and secure signed contracts within agreed timelines

    • Own and enforce the Editions commercial scorecard for new kitchens, profitability checks against P&L guidelines, launch package, site specificities, ensuring the process is applied consistently across the team

    • Steer the lead generation and pipeline process, mapping high-potential restaurants and cuisine gaps by site, and mobilising other commercial stakeholders to qualify interest

    • Lead commercial negotiations with business owners and C-suite operators, supporting proposals with a robust P&L rationale

  • P&L Ownership & Governance

    • Own a portion of the Editions P&L, accountable for revenue, profitability and the financial health of your perimeter

    • Set, own and deliver performance targets across occupancy, partner health, site profitability and Deliveroo output metrics

    • Run a clear operating rhythm on reporting, velocity, sign-to-live, occupancy and sales reviews, and use it to make decisions, not just to describe results

  • Kitchen Launches & Cross-functional Execution

  • Work with Site Managers, Food Safety, Compliance, Site Construction and Kitchen Layout teams to secure the successful build and launch of new kitchens

  • Coordinate with Global team on kitchen implementation, and with Marketing and Operations on launch packages, so that every opening lands on time and performs from week one

  • Manage and oversee project execution end to end, including B2B communication and cross-business-unit workshops

  • Propose process optimisation and automation: Deliveroo moves fast, and you will improve the processes that let Editions scale

  • Senior Stakeholder Management

    • Act as the senior point of contact and face of Deliveroo Editions for top restaurant partners, building trusted, long-term relationships and representing Deliveroo at partner events

    • Establish a strong operating rhythm with partners, including quarterly business reviews and monthly performance check-ins

    • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, providing strategic insights on Deliveroo, competitors and broader industry trends

  • Team Leadership: Support and coach your Account Managers and Sales Managers to build and execute strong commercial and operational plans, and to raise the standard of account management across the Editions network

What You’ll Need to Thrive

  • 7+ years working in commercially focused roles

  • Experience managing medium-sized commercial or account management teams

  • Highly analytical, with proven P&L ownership or strong financial decision-making experience

  • Solid project management skills, with a track record of delivering complex, cross-functional projects on time

  • Mix of both strategy and execution experience

  • Comfortable handling negotiations with business owners or C-suite operators

  • Effective collaborator, able to influence internal stakeholders across functions and geographies, including global teams

  • Relationship-building and communication skills whether face-to-face, through phone or email

  • Adaptable and comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment; proactive and creative problem solver

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a passion for food and operations

  • You will be in the field often, which will require travel (depending on the needs)

  • Previous general management experience, or experience running your own business would be desirable

  • Fluent in French and English is required

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving.

We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:


🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale
Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱See your impact, fast
Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership
environment.

🧠Grow through challenge and ownership
Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎A culture built for builders
High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

Our Global Structure

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!
